audit: Cohort pooled from many sources with very heterogeneous, non-standardised diagnosis labels (e.g. NOS, 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm, malignant', 'Glioma, malignant' as a catch-all) so diagnoses are mixtures and associations are label-dependent. 21 cases carry >100 mutations (up to 15,731), likely hypermutators or pooled/processing artifacts; they were excluded because they inflate passenger-gene counts (e.g. KMT2D hits came partly from one 5,370-mutation case). 124 cases have no mutations, so no-call versus wild-type is ambiguous. Many diagnoses have tiny n, so no reliable rare-diagnosis findings. ~438k gene-diagnosis tests were run; only the Bonferroni-surviving set is reported. Large genes (KMT2D, ASXL1, ARID1B) may reflect gene length and unmodelled covariates (age, site, source study); no per-gene length or batch correction was possible. I could not find ten genuinely novel, robust associations; the few non-established claims (PIK3R1 in pilocytic astrocytoma, ARID1B in RMS, ZMYM3 in glioma, ASXL1 in medulloblastoma) are hypothesis-generating and need independent replication. I did not inflate the list to reach the requested ten.
methods: Parsed cases and mutations; excluded 21 hypermutated cases (>100 mutations). For each gene and diagnosis (n>=5) with >=3 mutated cases and higher frequency than in all other tumors, ran one-sided-direction Fisher exact tests on case-level mutation status, with Bonferroni correction over all tests. Reported associations passing Bonferroni, plus a few borderline entries (ARID1B, KMT2D etc.) at lower probability; checked variant spectra for artifacts. Established status was judged from prior knowledge only.
